_comment: Connector-specific edits to GENERATED/authored files that a cli-printing-press reprint must NOT clobber. check_handfixes.py asserts every marker below is still present (and banned anti-patterns absent) and fails CI if a reprint dropped one. Provenance: project_pagerduty_onboard_traps.md (PR #48, 2026-06-06, press 4.22.0).

handfixes.summary: guide.md (vendored from the PagerDuty README) had ~96 ../../api-reference and ~9 openapiv3 deep-links into a non-shipped tree; repointed to developer.pagerduty.com and stripped to code text
handfixes.why: PagerDuty's source README carried ~96 [API Concepts](../../api-reference/<hash>...) links into a tree msp-skills doesn't ship plus ~9 [/path](openapiv3.json/...) OpenAPI spec deep-links - check_md_links FAILs. Fixed: repoint api-concepts links to the real vendor docs (https://developer.pagerduty.com/api-reference/, verified 200; check_md_links SKIPS http(s) so a 404 would slip) and strip openapiv3 spec deep-links to backtick code text. A reprint re-vendors the broken relative/openapiv3 links.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Fix belongs in the press README-vendoring step: rewrite or strip relative ../../ and openapiv3 deep-links that don't resolve in the shipped tree. Grep guide.md for `](../../` and `](openapiv3` after vendoring any new spec.

handfixes.summary: Analytics differentiator framed as offline / without the paid Analytics tier / no per-question call - NOT 'no API returns it' (which is false; the binary wraps the vendor Analytics API)
handfixes.why: Round-1 adversarial P1: README/SKILL/guide/page.json claimed MTTR-by-service / off-hours-pages were 'questions no single PagerDuty API call returns' - contradicted by the binary's own analytics commands that wrap the vendor Analytics API. The honest, defensible claim is 'offline / without the paid Analytics add-on / no live call per question'. A reprint of the authored marketing prose could reintroduce the false absolute claim.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Not press-encodable - a prose/marketing review rule. The fresh-context adversarial reviewer (not the gates) is the only thing that catches it; refines feedback_outcome_prose_must_match_command_output_fields.

handfixes.summary: Top-level manifest.json exists (press 4.22.0 emitted only tools-manifest.json; recovered from the prior scaffold commit so build-catalog stops failing)
handfixes.why: Press run 20260606-085517 emitted only tools-manifest.json, not the mcpb/DXT manifest.json onboard copies in step 3 - build-catalog.py failed 'missing manifest.json for skill'. Recovered from the prior partial-scaffold commit. A reprint from a press that still drops manifest.json reintroduces the missing-file failure; this ledger entry makes its absence a loud failure.

handfixes.summary: doctor probes a real GET endpoint with the real credential and refuses to dial a placeholder base_url, instead of calling any HTTP response 'reachable' and never checking the credential
handfixes.why: `doctor` is the command every SKILL, guide and docs page tells an operator to run to confirm the connector works, and it could not tell a working install from a broken one. It called any HTTP response to `GET /` "reachable" and rendered it green, so a base_url aimed at the vendor's web UI (where every API path 404s) and a token rejected with 401 on every call both produced an all-green report. On this connector family it also never probed the credential at all: it printed "present, not verified" and left the operator to guess. The mirror defect: a connector whose shipped base_url default is a placeholder dialled the placeholder host, and the DNS failure rendered as "FAIL API: unreachable" - telling a correctly-credentialled operator they were broken without naming the one variable that would fix it. Several placeholder hosts resolve through live wildcard DNS and answer real HTTP, so dialling one produced a confident green verdict against a stranger's server. Measured and gated by tools/maintainer/check_doctor_truth.py. See issue #282.

handfixes.summary: every operator credential this connector reads is declared on all three install channels: manifest.json (.mcpb), server.json (MCP Registry) and mcp-install.md (manual install)
handfixes.why: Issue #282 ('three live-verified connectors prompt for the wrong credentials'). A connector is installed through THREE independent channels that each carry their own copy of the credential list: manifest.json server.mcp_config.env (what the .mcpb bundle hands Claude Desktop, which has no shell profile, no config.toml and no export - so an undeclared variable is a variable nobody is ever asked for), server.json environmentVariables (the MCP Registry publish channel), and mcp-install.md's copy-paste JSON blocks plus its remote launch line (the manual path, which never touches the bundle at all). The fleet-wide audit found 60 of 65 connectors under-declaring 122 operator-facing variables in the manifest, 61 of 65 mcp-install.md pages omitting 125, and hudu's server.json missing the base URL its manifest marks required. For pagerduty the manifest gained: PAGERDUTY_BASE_URL. server.json gained: PAGERDUTY_BASE_URL. mcp-install.md's env blocks gained: PAGERDUTY_BASE_URL. manifest.json, server.json and mcp-install.md are ALL regenerated by /msp-skills-publish on an UPDATE or re-onboard, so without this ledger a regeneration silently drops every declaration and CI stays green (check_env_schema.py is wired --warn). The asserts below name the specific credentials, not a count, so dropping one and adding another cannot cancel out.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: cli-printing-press should emit server.mcp_config.env, the matching user_config prompts, server.json environmentVariables and mcp-install.md's env blocks from ONE declaration of the connector's operator-facing environment, so the three channels cannot be generated out of step. Until then check_env_schema.py compares all three and this ledger pins them.

handfixes.summary: The generator's hidden Cobra alias `create` is removed from the 3 commands listed in `why` whose POST deletes, cancels, disables, stops, rolls back or otherwise destroys or disrupts something, so `<parent> create` no longer runs them
handfixes.why: cli-printing-press gives a POST endpoint command the hidden alias `create`. On these commands the POST is destructive, so an agent that guessed the conventional verb (`<group> create`) ran the destructive call, and the alias appeared nowhere in help, agent-context or governance.md. Reproduced on origin/main 6416a241b against a local fake server: `maxio-cli subscriptions purge-json create sub_123 --ack 1` sent POST /subscriptions/sub_123/purge.json, `sentinelone-cli reports create` sent POST /reports/delete-reports and `tactical-rmm-cli agents shutdown create agent-42` sent POST /agents/agent-42/shutdown/. Fleet gate: tools/maintainer/check_command_tree.py, which walks the real cli.RootCmd() tree (137 such commands in 28 connectors on 6416a241b, 0 after). The canonical command names are unchanged; only the alias goes. A reprint re-adds it: remove it again. TestDestructiveCommandsDoNotAnswerToCreate fails while the alias is present. Commands here: business-services unsubscribe remove-business-service-notification-subscriber (POST /business_services/{id}/unsubscribe); event-orchestrations integrations migrate-orchestration (POST /event_orchestrations/{id}/integrations/migration); incident-workflows instances create-incident-workflow (POST /incident_workflows/{id}/instances).
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: emit the `create` alias only for operations that create something.

handfixes.summary: The learn journal keeps no text the operator typed in place of a declared name: the <PREFIX>_LEARN_SESSION override is stored as "o:" plus the same 64-bit SHA-256 hash the harness session ids get under "h:"; argv_shape records only flag names the invoked command declares (any other is a placeholder, nothing after "--" is a flag); the failed flag is an opaque identity; teach.log records counts, not raw arguments. A stored value that repeats a held credential is the shared credential kit's job now (credkit-wiring: every file and SQLite write goes through it).
handfixes.why: Press 4.34.0 and 4.34.2 (learn/journal.go.tmpl) return the override raw from JournalSessionKey, so a credential set there is written to journal-*.jsonl on every command, version included, and record every typed flag name, so a credential typed as a flag name (or after --) becomes an argv_shape key and the failed_flag; teach.log records the raw arguments of a teach with no --query; and a credential given as a profile name or description, a recall or teach query or operand, or feedback is stored as typed. Known limits: a guessable override or typed name can be confirmed by hashing guesses; entries an older build wrote stay until the 14-day retention deletes their segment; operator-named text that repeats no credential the process holds is a name and is kept. A reprint that drops these edits fails these asserts and TestJournalCredentialHardening; re-run tools/maintainer/apply_journal_hardening.py --slug <slug>. 2026-11-05 kit adoption: the RefuseHeld checks at each store and file (held_persist.go) are retired, replaced by the kit's file and SQLite sinks; the journal-shape asserts stay. Test: learn/journal_credential_hardening_test.go (the held pass holds through credkit.Hold).
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: learn/journal.go.tmpl should hash the LEARN_SESSION override as it hashes harness ids, and JournalArgvShape should take the invoked command's declared-flag lookup and record any other name as a placeholder, stopping at "--"; the failed flag should be an opaque identity; teach.log should not echo raw arguments; and every template that stores operator-named text should refuse one that repeats a held credential.

TestRefusedStartSaysWhy builds the binary and was seen failing (seen/mcp-startup-error-lost-seen-failing.log). tools/apply_credential_rules.py rewrites os.Exit( to exitMCP( in the generated main.go. handfixes.summary: Every on-call entry from GET /oncalls is stored as its own row: a transport beneath the origin pin stamps pp_oncall_key (a digest of escalation policy, level, schedule, user, start and end; null start/end of a permanent on-call read as empty) on each entry that lacks one, and /oncalls is keyed on it
handfixes.why: On-call entries carry no id (developer.pagerduty.com, List all of the on-calls). Without the key, sync either dropped every entry ("no extractable ID field", and the oncalls resource failed the sync) or, keyed on a fingerprint of top-level scalars (level, start, end), let two people on call at the same level and hours overwrite each other, so `oncall who` named one responder. handfixes.summary: A PAGERDUTY_API_KEY pasted as the whole header value (`Token token=<key>`, as PagerDuty's docs show it) is sent as is, never as `Token token=Token token=<key>`; its bare key is held like any other credential

handfixes.summary: 264 operations carry an x-pp-example (tools/spec_examples.py): the line the press itself synthesizes once the required Accept header is derivable, minus the defaulted --accept / --content-type flags. 294 of 422 endpoint commands show a runnable example (was 30)

The flag defaults to that value, so no command line needs it; making the header optional instead would stop sending it (optional header defaults are server assumptions). Spec-encoded: survives every reprint from this spec. Regenerate after a vendor-spec refresh: `spec_examples.py enum`, render, `spec_examples.py apply`. handfixes.summary: PagerDuty's list envelope members limit, offset and more are envelope metadata to the generated resource reader, so export, tail and the MCP export tool find the plural and write every record of every page
handfixes.why: The documented list envelope {"users": [...], "limit", "offset", "more", "total"} had three members the generated reader (resource_paths.go resourceSingleArray) did not know, so it found no item array: export users with 250 users wrote 1 record (page 1's envelope) and stopped. handfixes.summary: every generated cursor-paged command (PagerDuty documents next_cursor on each: audit records, automation actions and runners, incident workflow actions and triggers, workflow integrations and connections) reads next_cursor, so --all walks every page
handfixes.why: 13 generated commands passed an empty next-cursor path, so --all returned page 1 and stopped (pagination_signal_missing on stderr); users_oauth-delegations_list-user-delegations.go was generated with next_cursor. tools/apply_credential_rules.py sets it on every command paging on cursor (the class, not a file list). seen/cursor-all-stops-at-page-1-seen-failing.log; TestCursorListWalksEveryPage. (pagerduty 4.34.2 reprint)

handfixes.summary: An inner compressed stream with bytes before and after it, inside an outer stream's output, is read: a response carrying the API key that way is withheld whole. The kit reads a compressed stream at every byte offset of every view; this connector's own layer read only whole inner streams, so the class closes with the kit.
handfixes.why: Codex r1 [P1] secret in encoded output: GET /services returning a name that is base64 of raw DEFLATE three layers deep printed the API key, because the headerless search read text two streams deep and nothing in a stream's bytes. The class covers text or bytes between layers, with or without a header, in any mix (TestNestedStreamsAreReadToTheBound: 16 nestings, plus a random base64 blob and compressed public data not withheld). A headerless stream with bytes before or after it inside another stream's output is not read (followups.md). Test seen failing first: seen/r1-nested-stream-past-decoder-bound-seen-failing.log in the run dir. (pagerduty 4.34.2 reprint) 2026-11-05 kit adoption: closed by the kit, failing first through the built CLI on the pre-kit tree (.review/seen-nested-stream-fails.log) and passing with it (.review/nested-stream-passes.log).

handfixes.summary: oncall who applies every scope flag together: --service (its escalation policy), --escalation-policy, --team (the escalation policies the team owns in the synced escalation_policies, by id or name) and --user each narrow the result; a scope that resolves to nothing answers with nothing
handfixes.why: Codex r1 [P1] requested scope ignored: `oncall who --team PTEAM01` set only the label, so responders of every team answered for PTEAM01 (GET /escalation_policies documents each policy's teams); and --service replaced --escalation-policy instead of narrowing it. TestR1OncallWhoAppliesEveryScope (7 scope combinations through a real sync). Test seen failing first: seen/r1-requested-scope-ignored-seen-failing.log in the run dir. (pagerduty 4.34.2 reprint)

handfixes.why: Codex r1 [P1] simultaneous next responders dropped: GET /oncalls entries for PUSR001/PSCH001 and PUSR002/PSCH002 on one policy level showed one next responder, because the map was keyed on (policy, level). TestR1OncallWhoKeepsEverySimultaneousNextResponder (two schedules, two direct users, a later shift of the same schedule not shown). handfixes.why: Codex r1 [P1] removed permanent on-call read as current: sync only upserted, so a replaced permanent on-call stayed current after a fresh sync; the generated --full prune instead deleted history and future shifts. Hand file internal/cli/pagerduty_oncall_window.go, called from the GENERATED internal/cli/sync.go by an anchored edit (tools/apply_credential_rules.py). handfixes.summary: incidents timeline's detail carries every documented LogEntry field that says what happened (note, channel summary, event_details description, the changeset, the assignees, the notified user), else the entry's summary, else the channel type
handfixes.why: Codex r1 [P1] wrong field read from a documented response: an annotate_log_entry's note ("Do not restart the database.") showed as "website", because only channel.summary or channel.type was read. handfixes.summary: The /oncalls window reconcile deletes only after a walk that read from the first page on: a walk resumed from a saved position, or one the operator paged (--param offset or limit), deletes nothing
handfixes.why: Codex r2 [P1] partial pagination used as deletion evidence: the last page of `sync --param offset=1`, or of a walk resumed after a failure, proved nothing about the pages it never read, so still-valid on-call entries were deleted and `oncall who` dropped a responder. An operator's limit steps over entries the same way, because the walk advances by its own page size. TestR2PartialWalkIsNotDeletionEvidence (the reviewer's input, a limit, a resumed walk, and a whole walk that must still remove). Seen failing first: .review/seen-r2-partial-pagination-fails.log. handfixes.why: Codex r2 [P1] resolved ids confused with display names: a team's policy ids were also matched against other policies' labels, so `oncall who --team PTEAM01` answered with the responder of a policy named PEP0001 owned by another team. handfixes.summary: The shared credential kit (tools/maintainer/credkit, vendored at cli/internal/credkit) is wired by hand and replaces this connector's ported credential layer (held set, encodings, output chokepoint, secret funnel, history, outbound scan, store and journal refusals). internal/credwire/declarations.go holds the one Declarations literal; credkit.Start is the first statement of both mains and credkit.Exit ends them; every API request goes through client.OutboundGuard and the deliver, feedback and probe clients through credkit.Transport; the guard wraps the origin pin (api-origin-pinned), so every credential goes only to the base_url origin, and the MCP bearer and TLS key to none. Every file write outside the 0600 credential store and config file goes through the kit (cliutil.AtomicWriteCredentialFile is that declared exemption). The MCP server passes MCPTools, MCPIn, MCPOut and MCPHTTP and runs CLI children through RunCommand. Startup discovery reads the command line with credkit.FlagValues only and holds what every config, store and profile file the command line could mean carries; only the files the run reads are returned to the kit, so another file's base_url cannot become an allowed origin. A value the kit withholds prints "[credkit: withheld from <sink>: it carried a credential this program holds]".
handfixes.why: Retires, replaced by the kit (entries removed: the ledger's retired list only takes retirements fleet_handfixes.json backs): secret-echo-decoded-funnel, output-chokepoint, file-sinks-withheld, mcp-protocol-messages-withheld, network-sinks-withheld, startup-output-held-first, mcp-held-arguments-refused, undecoded-encodings-every-alignment, held-forms-in-every-encoding, response-credentials-held, config-file-holds-no-credential, every-text-encoding-withheld, outbound-split-parts-refused, auth-carrier-names-and-shapes-held, secure-container-is-credential, r1-holder-reads-every-part, r1-mixed-byte-escapes-decoded, r1-split-across-deliveries-withheld, held-value-case-folded, output-units-reassembled, preclose-holder-numbers-and-cookies, preclose-escape-fixpoint, preclose-split-across-processes-and-protocol, refuse-held-uses-connector-chokepoint, output-derived-and-scheme-forms-matched-whole, r1-short-value-encodings-withheld, r1-file-history-is-the-whole-file, r2-short-value-nested-encodings, r1-credential-split-across-deliveries, r1-decoder-bound-read-as-no-echo, r1-persistence-gate-narrower-than-chokepoint, credential-named-by-sibling-member, r1-credential-pair-identity-unheld, r1-command-line-config-unheld-at-startup, r1-short-held-value-inside-other-text, r1-secret-in-headerless-compressed-stream, r1-unreadable-history-read-as-empty, r1-check-then-append-not-serialized, spec-credential-under-a-generic-name, r1-mask-shaped-credential, r2-whitespace-credential, bb-whitespace-query-credential, r1-non-text-sql-binding-unheld, r1-persistence-gate-skipped-under-agentcookie, pagerduty-credential-names-exact, own-auth-descriptor-not-held, schema-describes-a-credential, r1-config-never-receives-a-credential. The connector-only layer grew per review round (2333 s of black-box tests, 19.6 s for agent-context with a key). One contract, one matcher and one set of sinks replace it, and a matcher fix reaches this connector by vendoring. The black-box suite internal/pagerdutyblackbox is retired with it: under the kit it did not finish in 890 s on this machine (the limit for keeping it is 300 s), and its corpus runs through class_harness.py, class_secret_corpus.py and the kit's fleet tests; its non-credential tests moved to internal/credwire (behaviors_test.go, kit_classes_test.go). Behavior changes: a credential a run reads from config.toml stays there (agentcookie's config store, a declared credential source under the contract's rule 7), and base_url keeps what a user wrote, its userinfo and query values held.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: generate the kit wiring (mains, one transport seam, file sinks, the SQLite driver, MCP framing, RunCommand) and the Declarations literal, so a reprint keeps them by construction.

handfixes.summary: Every SQLite handle goes through credkit.SQLDriver: internal/credsql registers the one driver and every sql.Open in store.go and platform/migration.go names it, the read-only openers included. The MCP sql tool's value cap moved from sqlite.Limit on a held connection to a DSN parameter credsql applies as each connection opens.
handfixes.why: A statement's text and bound values are a sink of their own, reads included. The retired withholding driver (r1-non-text-sql-binding-unheld) is replaced by the kit's.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: generate store, migration and MCP sql opens against one kit-wrapped driver name, and express the MCP sql value cap as a connection-open setting.

handfixes.summary: credkit.MCPHTTP writes every response the MCP HTTP server serves, refusals included: requireBearerAuthWithLimits runs a preflight that writes nothing, then credkit.MCPHTTP around a gate that answers the Origin, bearer and body-limit verdicts.
handfixes.why: With the kit wrapping only the inner handler a refusal answered outside it, and a refusal can repeat a piece of the bearer token (kaseya-vsa's review class, same template).
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: generate the MCP HTTP auth wrapper so its refusals are written by the inner, kit-wrapped handler and only a write-free preflight runs before credkit.MCPHTTP.

handfixes.summary: The kit's startup discovery holds what the run profile stores carry as a credential: a value under a credential flag's name or under base-url, every duplicate member included (cli.HoldProfileStores, called from credwire's credentialFiles). Free text in a profile is not a source, and profile save still takes no credential flag.
handfixes.why: profiles.json is a credential source the kit does not read for itself, and profile show printed a saved value. Declaring it in Files would hold every string in it, so a profile named "p" or a saved --limit 7 would refuse every later start.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: generate the profile store's hold from the credential flags the spec declares.

handfixes.summary: export writes one page of whole JSONL records per Write, or the whole JSON document in one Write, with no bufio, to --output and to stdout alike.
handfixes.why: The kit keeps a stream's whole context while a unit ends inside a JSON document and fails closed past 16 KiB, so the generated 4 KiB bufio writer withheld every record after about the 20th KiB of an ordinary export, and failed the run. Seen failing first: 250 users stopped at 20480 bytes with "writing export: [credkit: withheld from file...". Recorded for the kit in the adoption's findings; rocketcyber hit the same class.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Kit-side: keep context from the open document's start, not the whole stream, so a buffered JSONL writer passes. Press-side: generate export without a bufio writer over a kit sink until then.

handfixes.summary: agent-context encodes without HTML escaping (enc.SetEscapeHTML(false)), so its whole document, the auth descriptor included, prints with a key held, in about 3 s (19.6 s under the earlier layer).
handfixes.why: With the generated encoder the document's roughly 1000 \u003c and \u003e escapes spent the kit's whole decode budget, so with any key set the 453 KB output was one 76-byte notice. The same document without the escapes is clean. Recorded for the kit in the adoption's findings (contract: an exhaustion on ordinary output is a P2 fixed in the kit).
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: generate agent_context.go with SetEscapeHTML(false): the document is read by agents, never embedded in HTML.

handfixes.summary: GET /workflows/integrations prints the secrets_schema definition it returns: "Authentication Headers" keys a schema there, so it is not a declared ResponseFields name and the store keeps the definition as written.
handfixes.why: Replaces schema-describes-a-credential, which matched the schema's shape in the earlier layer. The kit holds only what is declared, so leaving the name out closes the class by construction.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: a credential classifier should separate a schema's property names from a credential's value.

handfixes.summary: sync wraps the event writer its parallel workers share in syncSerialWriter (internal/cli/sync_event_writer.go), so two workers never call Write on it at once.
handfixes.why: The generated sync hands cmd.OutOrStdout() (or ErrOrStderr() in machine output) to every --concurrency worker, and each writes sync_start, progress and error events. os.Stdout tolerates that; the writers --deliver (a mirror into a bytes.Buffer) and --receipt-file / --audit-dir (a running SHA-256) install do not, nor does an in-process caller's buffer: Windows CI on PR #655 panicked in bytes.Buffer.grow from syncResource, and go test -race found 28 races on veeam. TestSyncWorkerPoolSerializesEventWrites pins it. A reprint regenerates sync.go and drops the wrap; tools/maintainer/replay_handfixes.py re-applies it (fleet_handfixes.json sync-event-writer-serialized).
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side (mvanhorn/cli-printing-press#5369): the sync template should serialize the event writer its top-level worker pool shares, as its dependent path already does with lockedWriter.

handfixes.summary: the adaptive limiter's blind ramp raises only a rate the last Wait slept on, so sync's rate_rps reports a real pace
handfixes.why: On a header-less API the ramp multiplied the rate by 1.25 every 10 successes with no ceiling: mcp2's hubspot sync printed rate_rps 6.6e24 (about 2,500 requests), and after such a ramp a 429's halving could no longer slow a single request. A rate the requests never reach is no longer raised. Re-applied after a reprint by replay_handfixes.py (recipe limiter-paced).

handfixes.summary: a resource the vendor refuses this token (HTTP 403) is recorded as skipped and no longer holds store_status at partial; a resource that errored stays partial and is named.
handfixes.why: A 403 resource never completes, so its sync_state row stayed at 0 and store_status read partial for good after a clean exit 0 (#692). store_status now says complete_with_skips only when every other resource finished, and search, sql and sync_summary name what was skipped or failed. A reprint regenerates sync.go and mcp/tools.go and drops this; tools/maintainer/replay_handfixes.py re-applies it (fleet_handfixes.json sync-forbidden-not-partial).
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: sync should record a resource the vendor refuses separately from one that failed (not filed yet).

handfixes.summary: sync_progress reports measured rows per second (rows_per_sec, and rate_rps as the same value); the limiter's ceiling is limiter_ceiling_rps.
handfixes.why: The generated sync printed the adaptive limiter's ceiling as rate_rps and as req/s on the human line, so 4.9 was reported while the sync stored 33 rows a second (#694). A reprint regenerates sync.go and brings it back; tools/maintainer/replay_handfixes.py re-applies it (fleet_handfixes.json sync-progress-measured-rate).
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: the sync template should report a measured rate and name the limiter's ceiling separately (not filed yet).

handfixes.summary: sync writes at most one sync_progress line per resource every 5 seconds (the first page always reports; sync_complete carries the final count), instead of one per page.
handfixes.why: Every write to stdout or stderr costs a full credential check whatever its size, and sync wrote one progress line per page: 74% of hubspot sync's CPU at a real server's pace (#696). A reprint regenerates sync.go with one line per page; tools/maintainer/replay_handfixes.py re-applies the guard (fleet_handfixes.json sync-progress-throttled).

handfixes.summary: The <api>_search tool's description ends with the API's resource families (codeOrchSearchResources in internal/mcp/search_desc.go, from codeOrchEndpoints, capped at 300 characters).
handfixes.why: The generated description was the same in every connector and named no resource, so a host that ranks tools by words put other tools above <api>_search for "<api> <resource>" (#629; zammad_search ranked 13th of 45 for "zammad tickets").
